newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila accepts Nobel peace laureate's apology.
newsitem.headline: Manila accepts Nobel peace laureate's apology.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Tuesday accepted an apology from Nobel peace laureate Jose Ramos-Horta but said the government had not decided if it would allow him to visit the country in January.

The East Timorese resistance leader had wanted to visit the Philippines this month but the government refused him entry, saying his presence might disrupt the November 25 summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

Ramos-Horta wrote to the Philippine president last weekend apologising "for whatever personal discomfort" his abortive visit might have caused and said he wished to come to Manila in January on a teaching assignment.
Ramos told reporters he was accepting the apologies, "but we still reserve the right to make the decisions".

A group of non-governmental organisations critical of APEC had invited Ramos-Horta, joint winner of this year's Nobel Peace Prize with East Timorese Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo, to attend a meeting they planned to hold in parallel with the summit.
One of the APEC leaders expected to attend is Indonesian President Suharto.
Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the next year in a move never recognised by the United Nations.
